text:
I am a planner, not a programmer. Over the last few months I built an AI system around my project controls work, using Claude Code. This is every part of it, how it works, and what it gives me.

SCHEDULE

1. Baseline engine. The schedule is a model in Python: WBS, activities, logic, calendars, key dates. It is written straight into P6's XER tables, so P6 imports it as a new project. One baseline: 281 activities, 664 relationships, no constraints.

2. CPM checker. Before I import anything, a separate critical-path engine recalculates every date and float using P6's own rules: lags on the predecessor calendar, different snapping for milestones and tasks. It has to match before the file goes out.

3. Resource loading. Every activity takes quantity × manhour norm from the BOQ, by cost code. Composite rates are split back to source, so P6 and the BOQ agree on all 106 cost codes.

4. Curves. Custom 21-point P6 resource curves drive the S-curves, six commodity curves and the manpower histograms, all on the client's Saturday-to-Friday week.

5. Audit. A DCMA 14-point check and an import check run on every revision. Failures are listed activity by activity.

RECORDS, MAIL AND CONTRACTS

6. Records search. It reads 100+ daily reports, the issue log and the look-ahead plans, and tells me whether a delay event is actually recorded. Sometimes the honest answer is "it was never logged".

7. Outlook assistant. It searches my mailbox, reads the thread and its attachments, and drafts the reply for my review.

8. Contract Q&A. Retrieval over the contract and bid documents (RAG): it pulls the relevant clauses first, and every answer points to its clause or page.

What I have learned:
• The value is in the checks, not the speed. Two engines that must agree catch what one would miss.
• It makes confident mistakes. It once loaded piping erection months too early.
• It cannot replace knowing what is true on site.

This week I will go through the parts one by one.

Planners and project controls people: which of these eight would you use first, and which would you never trust to an AI?
